VI.description: The RemoteVI server: ONE While Loop\2C no event structure (docs\5Carchitecture.md\2C tools\5Cmock-server\5Cserver.mjs). Before the loop it creates a TCP listener on port (all interfaces)\2C obtains the notifier named stop notifier name and reads the name of VI for the title. Each iteration waits at most 5 ms for a connection and hands it to RemoteVI Handle Connection.vi (at most 8 WebSocket clients)\3B an upgraded connection gets the text messages title and viewonly 0 and joins the client list. POPUPS (docs\5Carchitecture.md\2C section Popups)\3A while a LabVIEW popup (menu\2C drop-down\2C graph palette popup) is open\2C LabVIEW's UI thread is in a modal loop and every VI Server UI call blocks\2C so each iteration first lists the popups with RemoteVI Find Popups.vi (Win32 only\3B class SysShadow\2C a menu's drop shadow\2C is left out of the overlay) - whenever a client is connected\2C a popup was open last time or the geometry is due. A popup (SysShadow included) that appears within 1 s after a client posted a button or key message was opened by a REMOTE user and is hidden on the host (RemoteVI Hide Window.vi\2C layered with alpha 0 - it stays open and clickable) and is hidden again on every iteration while it is open\2C because a menu's fade-in animation sets its alpha back to 255 (measured)\3B a popup opened at the host stays visible. The popups travel to the clients as OVERLAY messages (docs\5Cprotocol.md section 3.2)\3A at most every 1000/fps ms while a popup is open (or one was\2C to clear it) each popup is captured with RemoteVI Capture Window.vi (PrintWindow\2C so hidden\2C covered or off-screen popups are captured too)\2C PNG-encoded and placed at its window rectangle minus the panel origin - NOT clipped to the panel\2C bottom-most first\3B RemoteVI Overlay Encode.vi builds the message and it is written to every client only when it differs from the last one\2C an empty OVERLAY when the last popup has closed. A client that connects while a popup is open gets the current OVERLAY after its greeting. The loop caches the panel's geometry and window handle (RemoteVI Get Panel Geometry.vi before the loop\2C then every 500 ms and right after a popup closes\2C but only while NO popup is open) and the last panel capture. Every client is serviced (RemoteVI Service Client.vi) with the cached geometry\2C handle and the window handles of the open popups (a click on a popup borrows the host cursor until the popups change\2C RemoteVI Post Input.vi)\3B when at least one client is connected and 1000/fps ms have passed\2C a frame is made once and RemoteVI Send Frame.vi runs for each client. Without a popup the frame is a fresh capture (RemoteVI Capture Panel.vi)\2C which also becomes the cache. With a popup open NO VI Server call is made and the frame is the cached capture (the panel does not change while LabVIEW's UI thread is held). After a client posted a message that may open a popup (Service Client's clicked?) the loop also makes no VI Server UI call for 300 ms\2C so a popup that is still opening cannot catch FP.Get Image in its modal loop (measured\3A that froze the loop until the menu was closed on the host). A minimized panel is restored (RemoteVI Restore If Minimized.vi) when a client connects. Closed clients are dropped and their connections closed. The loop stops when the notifier delivers anything\2C when VI is no longer running (Execution\3AState checked once a second while no popup is open - so the server ends with your application)\2C or on a listener error other than a timeout. Then every connection and the listener are closed and the notifier released. Launched asynchronously by RemoteVI Start.vi.
